descriptions.text: Deribit has lost $28M from their hot wallets on the Ethereum and Bitcoin networks. As with all cases of “compromised keys”, only insiders can say for certain what caused the breach, but we have our usual suspects…

Crypto derivatives exchange Deribit tweeted that $28 million in losses from Deribit’s hot wallet was stolen, but customer funds were safe and the losses were covered by company reserves. According to the analysis of SlowMist MistTrack, the loss included 6967.65 ETH, 691 BTC and about 3.41 million USDC, and then the attacker exchanged USDC for 2143.95 ETH.

Deribit's hot wallet was compromised just before midnight UTC on 1 November 2022, leading to losses of approximately $28 million (BTC, ETH, USDC). Client assets and cold storage were unaffected and withdrawals were promptly suspended. Loss was covered by company reserves, with manual approvals and migration to Fireblocks hot wallets implemented as remediation. The root cause was a private key compromise of Deribit's hot wallet, enabling direct unauthorized withdrawal of assets by an attacker. The exact method of key exposure remains undisclosed.
